goal: Can you load this whole folder it’s a learning plan

steps.title: Mon: H100 numbers and the roofline ridge point
steps.why: Every later prediction (reduction bandwidth, softmax, RMSNorm) is built from these five numbers, so they come first.
gaps: Turning a hardware number into a lower bound on a specific kernel time is not yet practiced.
The ridge point differs between CUDA cores and tensor cores, and that split is not yet in the notes.

steps.title: Tue: Harris reduction slides, versions 1-3 on the H100
steps.why: Comes after Monday because the goal is a percent of the 3.35 TB/s peak, and before Wednesday because online softmax is parallelized with this same tree.
gaps: Why the cost of a tree step is counted in warps with work, not threads with work, is not yet worked through.
Bank conflicts in shared memory and coalescing in global memory are not yet told apart.
Why the 2007 warp-synchronous trick is unsafe on an H100, and what the shuffle version in reduce.py does instead, is not yet connected.

steps.title: Wed: online softmax, derive the rescale step
steps.why: Comes after Tuesday reduction because the parallel version of online softmax is a tree reduction over (max, sum) pairs.
gaps: The rescale factor exp(m_old - m_new) has not been derived by hand yet.
Why the merge operator being associative allows a tree reduction is not yet explained in own words.

steps.title: Thu: Triton fused softmax to one-pass online softmax
steps.why: Builds Wednesday derivation into code; needs the rescale step before writing the chunk loop.
gaps: The difference between one HBM pass and one pass over registers is not yet clear.
Mapping Triton programs and masks to CUDA blocks and bounds checks is not yet practiced.

steps.title: Fri: Nsight Compute numbers and the reduction in vLLM RMSNorm
steps.why: Last, because reading the profile and the production kernel both need the bandwidth targets from Monday and the reduction from Tuesday.
gaps: Reading DRAM throughput, achieved occupancy, and warp stall reasons together has not been done yet.
Recognizing a Harris-style reduction inside library calls like cub::BlockReduce is not yet practiced.
